newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's earnings rise on overseas strength.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's earnings rise on overseas strength.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. said Friday that earnings rose 10 percent in the third quarter as profit growth at restaurants outside the United States more than offset weak domestic results.

The world's largest restaurant chain said net income rose to $440.6 million, or 62 cents a share, in the quarter, from $400.1 million, or 56 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. Revenues grew 8 percent to $2.77 billion from $2.58 billion.

The Oak Brook, Ill.-based company said operating earnings fell 5 percent in the quarter in the United States while revenue rose just 1 percent. The decline in operating income reflected tough competition and higher expenses, it said.
"Our U.S. restaurants are operating in a complex, dynamic and difficult marketplace and recent operating performance has fallen short of our goals," Chairman Michael Quinlan said in a statement.
A recent management reorganization was meant to help address the disappointing results, he said.
Outside the United States, operating earnings grew 11 percent in the quarter as revenue jumped 13 percent.
It said growth in earnings was strongest in Hong Kong, England, Italy, Spain, Sweden and Taiwan. Results in Mexico remained weak due to the sluggish economy, it said.
McDonald's had 11,852 restaurants, including smaller outlets, in the United States at Sept. 30, up 8 percent from a year earlier, and 8,139 in other countries, a rise of 26 percent.
The results were a penny shy of the 63 cents a share forecast by analysts, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
McDonald's stock fell 37.5 cents to $45.875 in trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
